TC1.Test Description: Verifies default register values and read/write behavior across GPIO registers using defined address and mask arrays.
TC1.Remarks: Some addresses are intentionally skipped for reset and write/read checks. Default value comparison masks off bit 0 before evaluating.
TC1.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the test environment and access the GPIO register set.
2) For each listed register address, skip entries marked for reset-skip or not readable; read the value and compare with the expected default after masking bit 0.
3) For each of six data patterns, write the masked data to each writable register that is not skipped; then read back with the read mask and compute the expected value based on write/read masks and defaults.
4) For each register, compare the read value with the computed expected value and record mismatches.
5) Report overall pass if there are no default mismatches and no write/read mismatches; otherwise report failure.
TC1.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Default read check: Each readable register equals the expected default after masking bit 0; any mismatch results in failure.
- Read/write check: For each pattern and register, the read-back equals the expected value derived from masks and defaults; any mismatch results in failure.
- Overall result: Pass if both default and read/write checks have zero failures; otherwise fail.

   3.2 For each j=0..5, set data_wr = chk_val[j].

       - If data_rd == exp_val, pass; else increment wr_fail_cnt and print mismatch with addr, expected, read.

TC2.Feature: neie (Reset: 0x0) Negative edge interrupt enable; 1 - Enable interrupt when falling edge (neg edge) is detected on gpio pin; 0 - Disable interrupt on neg-edge detection
TC2.Test Description: Verifies that falling edges on GPIO pins trigger interrupts when negative-edge detection is enabled and that status and clears work correctly.
TC2.Remarks: Interrupt line and sysreg routing depend on compile-time selection of GPIO0 or GPIO1. Each pin is exercised with a bounded timeout using a software pending flag.
TC2.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the appropriate interrupt line in the controller and route the system register interrupt output.
2) Drive all pads high by writing to 0xA0243ffc to establish a known starting level.
3) For each of 32 pins, configure the corresponding control register for input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and clear per-pin raw status.
4) For each bit, clear group raw status, enable only that bit in the group enable register, arm the pending flag, then generate a falling edge by toggling 0xA0243ffc from all ones to all ones with the target bit cleared.
5) Wait with a timeout for the interrupt service routine to complete; record a timeout as a failure.
6) In the ISR, confirm the pin input reflects a low level, the group status bit is set for the pin, clear per-pin raw status, clear the group raw status for the bit, verify the group status is cleared, clear the system interrupt source, and clear the interrupt in the controller.
TC2.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Interrupt occurrence: For each pin, a single interrupt is observed after the induced falling edge; if no interrupt before timeout, the test fails for that pin.
- Pin state check: The input state for the serviced pin is low after the falling edge; a non-low state fails.
- Status handling: The group status reflects the pin before clear, and reads as zero after per-pin and group clears; any residual status fails.
TC2.Hidden_Test_Description: Directed interrupt test that enables negative-edge interrupts per GPIO (8..39). It configures input mode (doe=1), enables negedge (neie=1), clears raw per-pin (iclr=1), enables group bit, induces a falling edge via 0xA0243ffc toggling, and verifies ISR behavior including DIN check, group status set/clear, sysreg raw clear, and GIC clear, with a bounded wait using int_pend and timeout.

- Uses GIC interrupts 87 (GPIO0) or 88 (GPIO1) under compile-time guards.
- Uses 0xA0243ffc to drive pad levels: set to 0xFFFFFFFF, then ~bit to create a 1->0 transition for pin (i+8).
- Per-pin control register is written with (1<<20 | 1<<18 | 1<<16) corresponding to doe=1, neie=1, iclr=1.
- Group raw pre-clear (MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1) and per-bit enable (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1) precede stimulus to avoid races.
- Timeout loop waits while int_pend is set; ISR clears int_pend to 0.
TC2.Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure:
1. Initialization:
   - test_err = 0.
   - Conditionally enable IRQ 87 (GPIO0) or 88 (GPIO1) via GIC_EnableIRQ.
   - Conditionally enable sysreg interrupt by writing MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR or LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR.
   - Write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC to drive all pads high.
2. Configure per-pin for input and negedge with clear:
   - For i=0..31: addr1 = (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4); write (1<<20 | 1<<18 | 1<<16); wait_on(10).
3. For each bit i=0..31:
   - wr_val = 1u << i.
   - Pre-clear group raw: write MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 = wr_val.
   - Enable only this bit: write MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 = wr_val; wait_on(10).
   - Arm wait: int_pend = 1.
   - Create falling edge: write 0xA0243FFC = 0xFFFFFFFF; wait_on(30); write 0xA0243FFC = ~wr_val.
   - Timeout wait: timeout=5000; while (int_pend && timeout--) wait_on(10); if timeout==0: log timeout error for GPIO(i+8) and test_err++.
4. Finish: finish(test_err).

   - If (rdata & 0x1) != 0 then test_err++ (DIN should be 0 after negedge).
   - If (rdata & 0x2) != 0x0 then:
       * rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1); if ((rdata_grp & local_wr) == 0) test_err++.
       * raddr2 = (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4); write (1<<20 | 1<<16) to clear per-pin raw while keeping doe=1.
       * write MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 = local_wr to clear group raw.
       * rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1); if (rdata_grp != 0x0) test_err++.
       * Conditionally write MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 = LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR (and GIC_ClearIRQ(87)) or corresponding GPIO1 path; else branch: test_err++ if raw not set.

TC3.Feature: peie (Reset: 0x0) Positive edge interrupt enable; 1 - Enable interrupt when rising edge (pos edge) is detected on gpio pin; 0 - Disable interrupt on pos-edge detection
TC3.Test Description: Verifies that rising edges on GPIO pins trigger interrupts when positive-edge detection is enabled and that group status and clears function correctly.
TC3.Remarks: All pins are enabled together for group interrupts. The test uses a software pending flag and timeout per pin to avoid hangs.
TC3.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the appropriate interrupt line in the controller and route the system register interrupt output.
2) For each of 32 pins, enable positive-edge detection in the corresponding control register.
3) Set all pins to input mode using the group IO control registers.
4) Enable all bits in the group interrupt enable register.
5) For each bit, drive low via 0xA0243ffc, arm the pending flag, then drive high to generate a rising edge; wait with a timeout for the interrupt.
6) In the ISR, read group status, mask group interrupts, clear per-pin raw status for all pins, verify group status is cleared, clear the system interrupt source, and re-enable group interrupts.
TC3.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Interrupt occurrence: For each pin, an interrupt occurs after the induced rising edge; if no interrupt before timeout, the test fails.
- Status handling: Group status shows a non-zero value during service and reads as zero after all clear operations; any residual status fails.
